result.title: Quality, Not Just Outcome: A Structural Scoring Framework for Selecting Coding-Agent Trajectories for Supervised Fine-Tuning
result.summary: Open coding agents are commonly trained through supervised fine-tuning on interaction trajectories whose final patches pass the benchmark test suite. However, this outcome-level filtering criterion ignores process quality: trajectories that eventually succeed may still contain inefficient interaction patterns such as repetitive file inspection, unstable tool usage, or delayed modification behavior, all of which become part of the imitation target. We propose TQS (Trajectory Quality Score), a structural scoring framework for coding-agent trajectories that operates directly on trajectory structure, requires no LLM judge, and runs in linear time. TQS characterizes trajectory quality through structural signals organized around structured convergence: information focus, intent--action alignment, and policy dynamics. Using 155,144 successful trajectories from a public open-license corpus, we rank trajectories by TQS and fine-tune coding agents on filtered subsets. Models trained on top-ranked trajectories consistently outperform those trained on random or bottom-ranked subsets on SWE-Bench-Verified. Our results suggest that process-level trajectory quality is an important factor in coding-agent supervision and that structural trajectory filtering provides an effective and scalable alternative to LLM-based data selection.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TQS 结构化评分框架，用信息聚焦、意图—动作对齐、策略动态等轨迹结构信号，无需 LLM 评判、线性时间地对编码智能体轨迹打分，并在约 15.5 万条成功轨迹上筛选子集做监督微调，top 子集在 SWE-Bench-Verified 上优于随机或底部子集。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「只看结果、不看过程」的诊断与过程级轨迹结构打分，可能为 LVR 的轨迹训练与监督筛选提供线索：可核查这类结构信号（收敛性、重复行为）能否用于筛选 latent 推理轨迹或评估推理过程质量；但对象是纯文本编码轨迹，无视觉状态与 latent 生成，迁移性待核查。
